MultiNorm

Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data

Website | Installation | Input requirements | Quick start | Vignette | Citation

Overview

MultiNorm is an R package for spatially aware normalisation of multi-slice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data.

MultiNorm decomposes observed gene expression variation into biological and technical components. The method aims to reduce unwanted technical variation while preserving biologically meaningful expression patterns and variations within and across tissue slices.

It uses pre-identified biological regions, referred to as niches, to encourage consistency of average biological signals across matched regions in different tissue slices.

Installation

The development version of MultiNorm can be installed directly from GitHub:

# Install remotes if required
install.packages("remotes")

# Install MultiNorm
remotes::install_github("Lahiru-lsb/MultiNorm")

Load the package:

library(MultiNorm)

Input requirements

MultiNorm accepts a named list of SpatialExperiment objects, where each object represents an individual tissue slice. The spe_list must be arranged according to the spatial order of the tissue slices.

Each object should contain:

  • A raw gene expression count matrix.
  • Two-dimensional spatial coordinates stored in the spatialCoords slot.
  • Spot-level biological niche annotations.
  • A common set of genes across tissue slices.

Niche annotations should represent biologically comparable regions across slices. These annotations can be obtained using spatial clustering methods or from existing biological annotations.

Quick start 

library(MultiNorm)

# Normalise multiple tissue slices
norm_spe <- MultiNorm(
  spe_list = spe_list,
  niche_col = "niche"
)

By default, MultiNorm returns a list of normalised SpatialExperiment objects.

# Access the first normalised tissue slice
norm_slice1 <- norm_spe[[1]]

# Access normalised gene expression
SummarizedExperiment::assay(norm_slice1, "logcounts")

An example with user-specified parameters is shown below:

norm_spe <- MultiNorm(
  spe_list = spe_list,
  niche_col = "niche",
  spot_frac = 0.5,
  df_bio = c(6, 6),
  df_tech = c(3, 3),
  lambdaC = 10000,
  lambda1 = 0.01,
  lambda2 = 2,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Returning fitted model parameters

Fitted model parameters can be returned together with the normalised data by setting return_fit = TRUE.

result <- MultiNorm(
  spe_list = spe_list,
  niche_col = "niche",
  return_fit = TRUE
)

norm_spe <- result$norm_spe
fit <- result$fit

Vignette

A detailed demonstration of MultiNorm is provided using four human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) tissue slices from the spatialLIBD package.

The vignette covers:

  1. Downloading and preparing spatial transcriptomics data.
  2. Performing basic quality control.
  3. Selecting common highly variable genes.
  4. Identifying biologically similar niches across slices.
  5. Applying MultiNorm.
  6. Comparing library size distributions before and after normalisation.

To access the installed vignette:

vignette("MultiNorm", package = "MultiNorm")

The vignette is also available through the MultiNorm documentation website.
